models_evaluated: GPT-5 with custom prompt plus RAG
GPT-5-nano with custom prompt plus RAG

links.outcome: Pairwise rater preference for RAG-grounded vs non-RAG LLM pathology explanations
links.effect: GPT-5-nano with RAG scored 0.40 higher than without (P=.02; 60% win rate); GPT-5 RAG vs no RAG not significant; GPT-5_p_rag only config significantly preferred over pathologists (0.33; P=.04).
links.quote: Although the difference between GPT-5_p_rag and GPT-5_p was not statistically significant, GPT-5-n_p_rag scored 0.40 points higher than GPT-5-n_p ( P = .02; 60% win rate).

links.outcome: LLM configurations compared with pathologist-written explanations on same questions
links.effect: GPT-5_p_rag met noninferiority (Δ=1.5) and was significantly preferred over pathologist responses (58% win rate, P=.04); GPT-5-n_p performed worse (36% win rate, P<.001).
links.quote: Among all configurations, GPT-5_p_rag achieved the highest ability estimate and was the only model statistically significantly preferred over pathologist-written responses (difference, 0.33; P = .04; 58% win rate).

links.outcome: Agreement between LLM grader and pathologist graders on rubric scores
links.effect: LLM evaluator scored LLM-generated responses 1.20 points higher than pathologists (P<.001), but did not differ for pathologist-written responses (-0.25; P=.67).
links.quote: In contrast, for LLM-generated responses, the LLM evaluator assigned higher scores than pathologist evaluators (paired mean difference, 1.20; P < .001) ( Table 1 ).
